fixes.explanation: Grudges are a human thing, but Malachi doesn't name them here. He asks why "…we break faith with one another…" (Malachi 2:10). Breaking faith means not keeping your word to someone. The question comes right after "Do we not all have one Father?"

Rumors get around fast, but they're not named in this verse. Malachi asks, "Why then do we break faith with one another…" (Malachi 2:10). The words he uses are "break faith," and that's the answer here. The question comes right after "Do we not all have one Father?"

True! The people ask "Why?" and Malachi answers, "It is because the LORD has been a witness between you and the wife of your youth…" (Malachi 2:14). The LORD is the witness between a man and his wife. I think that's a heavy thing to hear, and Malachi says it straight.

It's actually True. Malachi says, "It is because the LORD has been a witness between you and the wife of your youth, against whom you have broken faith…" (Malachi 2:14). That's his answer to their "Why?" The LORD has been a witness between the man and his wife. I think this one lands hard.

Neighbor is a good word, but it's not the one here. Malachi says she is "…your companion and your wife by covenant." (Malachi 2:14). She's named as a companion and a wife, not a neighbor. Even I'd say that's a bigger deal than lending someone a cup of flour.

Wealthy doesn't make the list. Malachi says, "Because He seeks godly offspring." (Malachi 2:15). The word in that verse is godly, not wealthy. That's the reason the text gives for why the LORD made them one.

Wealth doesn't come up in this verse, friend. The LORD, the God of Israel, says, "For I hate divorce…" (Malachi 2:16). That's the one thing He names. I think this is a heavy verse, so it's worth reading slowly.
